5.1 Dissolve 2 g of dried sample in a platinum dish, using 20 ml of concentrated nitric acid and add hydrofluoric acid droplvise until the Heat to complete dissolution and evapovigorous reaction has subsided. i\dd 30 ml of concentrated nitric acid and a fe\v ml of rate to 101~ bulk. . . dilLl(e potassium pcrmanganate solutron till permangnnate colour persists. 3

IS : 1559 ( Part

IV ) - 1982

Boil and destroy excess potassium permanganate solution with sodium nitrite solution. Dilute to about 50 ml, filter and wash. Collect the filtrate and washings in a 500-ml conical flask. Add about 2 g of boric acid to the solution in the flask and heat to dissolve. Add ammonium hydroxide ( 50 percent ) till the precipitate formed difficultly dissolves. Dissolve the precipitate in concentrated nitric acid added dropwise finally providing 5 ml in excess. Heat the solution to boiling on a hot-plate and then keep it aside to attain a temperature of 8O'C. Add now 30 to 35 ml of freshly filtered ammonium molybdate solution and shake vigorously for about 15 minutes. Keep the solution for settlement for about halfan-hour. 5.2 Filter the precipitate of ammonium phospho-molybdate on a paper pulp pad transferring all the precipitate from the flask into the pad by washing with cold neutral potassium nitrate wash solution. Wash the precipitate on the pad three times with cold nitric acid wash solution and then with cold neutral potassium nitrate wash solution again until the washings are no longer acid to phenolphthalein ( see Note ). Transfer the precipitate to the original conical flask where the phosphorus was first precipitated. Add a known excess of sodium hydroxide solution. Titrate the excess of sodium hydroxide solution with standard nitric acid by using phenoIphthalein as indicator. Take a blank of sodium hydroxide solution used in the experiment and from the difference calculate the percentage of phosphorus as given in 6.
NOTE - 10 ml of final washings collected in a test tube should give pink colour with phenolphthalein by a drop of sodium hydroxide solution of approximately @075 N. Normally the precipitate is washable free from acid by giving about 5 to 6 washings.
